extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) subject to USPTO professional conduct rules; OED staff; counsel handling USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order approving a settlement resolving disciplinary action against a registered practitioner, stating jurisdiction, stipulated facts, legal conclusions, sanctions, conditions for reinstatement, publication, and procedural mechanisms for enforcement. It exemplifies how the OED and USPTO Director impose and document discipline for practitioner misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional statutory and regulatory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order invokes these statutory/regulatory provisions as the basis for the Office's power to approve settlement agreements and impose discipline. Any disciplinary action requires reliance on the cited authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: At all times relevant, the respondent is subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct set forth at 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101 through 11.901.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that registered practitioners are governed by the Rules and may be sanctioned for violations of those Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conviction reflecting adversely on fitness (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A conviction of a crime that reflects adversely on a practitioner's fitness as a practitioner in other respects violates 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The respondent's felony Menacing (Domestic Violence) and misdemeanor Child Abuse convictions were found to violate § 11.804(b); the Final Order cites those convictions as the basis for the legal conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim suspension authority (37 C.F.R. § 11.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may issue an interim suspension pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document notes the Office issued a Final Order placing the respondent on interim suspension under § 11.25 on April 1, 2022, illustrating use of interim suspension where warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum suspension sanction and effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and non-patent law for a minimum of twelve (12) months, with suspension considered to have commenced on a specified date (here, February 28, 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order prescribes the length of suspension and fixes the commencement date; settlement agreements can set minimum suspension periods and retroactive commencement dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition timing and OED discretion (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may submit a petition for reinstatement no earlier than a specified date (here, January 31, 2023), but the OED Director is not required to act on or grant reinstatement prior to completion of the suspension; reinstatement is governed by 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies earliest filing date for petition and emphasizes the OED Director's discretion to deny, delay, or condition reinstatement despite petition timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of suspension until affirmative reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice before the USPTO until the OED Director grants Respondent's petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the minimum suspension term elapses, active suspension continues until affirmative administrative reinstatement is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary period conditions and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a probationary period commencing on the date the Final Order is signed and continuing until eighteen (18) months after a decision by the OED Director granting reinstatement, or until termination of the respondent's criminal probation, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation period may be tied to both administrative reinstatement timing and external criminal probation, and extends well beyond the minimum suspension in some circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to report criminal probation violations to OED
rubrics_metrics.description: Any finding that respondent violated his criminal probation shall be considered prima facie evidence of a violation of his USPTO probation, and respondent is required to report in writing to OED any finding that he violated the terms of his criminal probation within seven (7) days of such finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an affirmative reporting duty with a strict (7-day) timeline and treats criminal-probation violations as presumptive grounds for further USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause (OSC) procedure and respondent response period
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the respondent failed to comply during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to respondent's last address of record, and grant respondent fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies service, timing, and the administrative step before recommending further suspension to the USPTO Director; establishes procedural due process steps for alleged probation violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED referral to USPTO Director for additional suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If after the 15-day response period the OED Director remains of the opinion that respondent failed to comply, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director (i) the OSC, (ii) respondent's response (if any), and (iii) argument and evidence supporting the OED Director's view, and request immediate suspension for up to an additional one (1) year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the escalation path and the materials the OED must forward to obtain additional administrative suspension from the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrete discipline for misconduct underlying OSC
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing prevents the OED Director from seeking discrete discipline for any misconduct that formed the basis for an Order to Show Cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED may pursue separate disciplinary proceedings (in addition to OSC-driven suspension) based on the same underlying misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of suspension does not stay suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director suspends the respondent pursuant to the OSC referral, any review of the suspension shall not operate to postpone or hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative or judicial review does not automatically stay the effective suspension period ordered by the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with specific reinstatement/withdrawal rules (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References specific regulatory provisions practitioners must follow concerning surrender/withdrawal (11.58) and reinstatement (11.60); compliance with these regs is a condition of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice of suspension and probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final disciplinary actions are publicly posted online and summarized in the Official Gazette; the order includes a model notice text to be used for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of procedural rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent waives all rights to seek reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and waives the right otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of a settlement, respondents may waive statutory/regulatory review and appeal rights; such waivers are explicitly recorded in the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement can resolve cost allocation by having each party bear its own costs rather than imposing recovery of fees or costs against the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of mitigation and aggravation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order notes mitigating considerations (respondent promptly reported his conviction to OED, cooperated with OED's investigation, has never been subject to prior USPTO discipline, and participates in assistance programs) and reserves the Office's right to consider the record in future matters as an aggravating factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation, self-reporting, lack of prior discipline, and participation in assistance programs are relevant mitigating facts; the Office may nevertheless treat the record as aggravating in future proceedings or to rebut representations by respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agreement resolves all disciplinary action by the USPTO arising from the stipulated facts set forth in the Order, and the USPTO Director's approval makes the Agreement a Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement can fully resolve current disciplinary claims based on stipulated facts, subject to acceptance by the USPTO Director; the Final Order memorializes the settlement terms and sanctions.
